title: Fever with low white cells (febrile neutropenia)

items: Febrile neutropenia is a fever together with a low count of white blood cells (neutrophils), which fight infection.
It is an emergency, because infection can spread quickly when the count is low.
Fever of 38.3 degrees C or more in one reading, or 38 degrees C or more sustained over an hour.
Signs of infection may be hidden when the count is very low.
Blood cultures from the line and from a vein.
Chest X-ray, urine tests, and a risk score to decide where you are treated.
Antibiotics are started quickly, usually into a vein.
Your team will decide if you can be treated as an outpatient or need admission.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not wait. Go to the hospital straight away if you have a fever and are on treatment that lowers your white cells.
Tell staff about your condition whenever you arrive.
Your oncology team will review your counts and plan.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever of 38.3 degrees C or more (emergency: immediate antibiotics are required)
Low blood pressure, shivering, or feeling faint
Confusion, breathlessness, or feeling very unwell with signs of infection
